To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dynamical fermions can be used to study mass generation in massless QED_2+1, and that the sign problem is under control.

the chiral symmetry breaking transition in massless QED_2+1 can be studied with explicit dynamical staggered fermions using the sign problem reducing technique of Ref. \cite{Kanamori:2010sc}, and that our results are consistent with previous studies.

we have demonstrated that a recently developed algorithm to reduce the sign problem can successfully also be applied to the QED_3 model, and that our results are in agreement both with the strong coupling expansion, and with Euclidean simulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether or not the chiral symmetry of QED in (1+1) dimensions is spontaneously broken.
the study of the phase structure of QED_3.
the dynamical mass generation of QED in (3+1) dimensions and QED in (1+1) dimensions, as well as QED in (4+1) dimensions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the massless QED_2+1 is a confining theory, with dynamical mass generation, and with a mass gap.
we have demonstrated that the dynamical fermion sign problem is not a show-stopper for Hamiltonian lattice simulations of massless QED_ 3.
dynamical fermions are essential for a correct description of dynamical mass generation, and that the sign problem can be overcome for this system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mass gap of QED_3 in the chiral and continuum limits is zero.
we have demonstrated that the dynamical mass generation of the fermions in QED3 is robust and that the sign problem can be reduced to an acceptable level for this system.
the dynamical mass generation is a smooth transition from the massless to massive phase, and the mass generation is a second order phase transition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fermion sign can be reduced significantly, allowing for the simulation of this model with dynamical fermions.
the chiral symmetry of the theory is not restored for large fermion masses.
the fermion sign-problem is not an obstacle to the study of dynamical mass generation.
